tags.qa_notes: Deep re-audit 2026-09-25. Re-fetched scubastlucia.com/diving/ live today: 'steep slope covered by many soft corals' with 'a great profusion of fish life' at the base of Petit Piton, drift dive, Superman II filming location - reconfirms prior pass exactly. PADI's soft corals/sponges/grunts/parrotfish and stingray/turtle sightings still stand (not independently re-fetched today, carried forward). NEW: stolentime.com (fresh domain today) reports 'whale-shark and humpback-whale have been observed passing by' - a single-source, hedged ('have been observed') claim not corroborated by any other source; included in the markdown explicitly as an occasional/rare single-source report rather than a typical sighting, per the flag-uncertainty rule. Depth 50m retained; no conflicting figure found today.

Deep re-audit 2026-09-25. Re-fetched scubastlucia.com/diving/ live today: plateau 5-25ft dropping to 140ft (42m) at the outer edge, 150+ fish species, moray eels, parrotfish, blennies, crabs, and big schools of needlefish (blennies and crabs are newly reconfirmed today, added to the marine-life list). PADI's blog today separately describes an unidentified 'Loch Ness Monster'-style creature nicknamed 'The Thing' at this site; this is explicitly framed by the source itself as folklore/legend, not a confirmed species sighting, so it has been excluded from the marine-life section per the anti-hallucination policy on legend-style filler. Depth field kept at 20m for the beginner-accessible plateau; the 42m drop-off remains noted separately in the markdown as a non-beginner extension.

Deep re-audit 2026-09-25. NEW independent source found and used today: divejourney.io's 'Anse Cochon' dive-spot profile independently corroborates the four-pinnacle formation ('rise abruptly from the depths to within a few metres of the surface... trumpetfish, filefish and seahorses... amongst whip corals and gorgonians') and the broader Anse Cochon topography (reef/boulders/walls/pinnacles all on one dive, max depth 12-18m matching our 18m field), and adds anemone crabs as a newly confirmed shallow-water species. scubastlucia.com's live listing reconfirms seahorses, scorpionfish, and cleaner shrimp in the shallow areas exactly as before. smmainc.com and divesaintlucia.com again returned no usable content on direct fetch today (403 / empty) so their prior corroboration (hawksbill turtles, flounder) is carried forward, not freshly re-verified this cycle.

Deep re-audit 2026-09-25. Three new independent sources found today: caribbean-diving.com/dive-sites/keyhole-pinnacles (barrel sponges, tube corals, black/orange gorgonian fans; trumpetfish, groupers, snappers, filefish, seahorses, pufferfish - snapper and pufferfish are new confirmed additions), stolentime.com ('trumpet fish, filefish, and sometimes seahorses. Larger fishes such as grouper, jack and snapper' - independently corroborates snapper and adds jack), and divejourney.io (trumpetfish, filefish, seahorses among whip corals/gorgonians, matching existing description). REVERSAL: jack and snapper were removed in the 2026-07-03 pass as unconfirmed; two independent fresh sources now confirm snapper and one confirms jack, so both are restored. caribbean-diving.com also mentions a single hedged claim ('people have reported seeing... for instance') of whale sharks and sunfish at this site - not corroborated elsewhere; included in the markdown explicitly labeled as a rare, single-source, unconfirmed report rather than a typical sighting.

Deep re-audit 2026-09-25. scubastlucia.com live fetch today reconfirms the crescent-shaped reef dropping from a 40ft (12m) plateau to over 150ft (45m+), pillar coral, barrel sponges, hawksbill and green turtles - unchanged from prior pass. stolentime.com (new domain) independently names 'Turtle Reef' and confirms the same shallow-to-deep pillar-coral/barrel-sponge structure but adds no new species beyond a vague 'plenty of other creatures.' Parrotfish, blue chromis, damselfish, moray eels, and spiny lobsters remain carried forward from an earlier pass and could not be independently re-verified on a live source for a second consecutive audit cycle (2026-07-03 and 2026-09-25); flagged here for a future pass to either re-confirm from a live source or remove.

Deep wreck-history re-audit 2026-09-25, 6 independent sources fetched/searched today. RECONFIRMED: 165-foot freighter (scubastlucia.com, islanderkeys.com, padi.com, divingaway.com all agree on 165 feet), sunk as a deliberate artificial reef by St Lucia's Department of Fisheries; scubastlucia.com's own live listing today states 'sunk in October 1986' directly. SINKING-YEAR CONFLICT NOTED: divingaway.com states 1985 versus four other sources (scubastlucia.com, islanderkeys.com, caribbean-diving.com, padi.com) stating 1986 - the 1986 date is treated as the well-corroborated figure and the single 1985 outlier is flagged in the markdown rather than silently dropped. Depth range reconfirmed at roughly 18-22m/60-72ft across sources, deck near 9-12m. Marine life substantially expanded with fresh sourcing: moray eels (3 sources), lobsters (3), turtles (2: islanderkeys.com, divingaway.com), spider crabs (2), shrimp/coral-banded shrimp (2), French/angelfish (2: islanderkeys.com, padi.com), red snapper and barracuda and tuna/pelagics (islanderkeys.com), scorpionfish (caribbean-diving.com), frogfish (scubastlucia.com), and octopus/nudibranchs (divingaway.com, single-source but site-specific). stolentime.com independently corroborates a juvenile-fish nursery habitat with Nassau grouper, queen angelfish and French angelfish specifically named - a third source for the nursery-habitat claim.

Deep re-audit 2026-09-25. scubastlucia.com live fetch today reconfirms schooling fish, creole wrasse, bar jack, and 'occasionally the southern sennet' at the base of Gros Piton - unchanged. NEW: stolentime.com lists a site named 'Gros Piton Reef' whose description ('schooling fish, particularly creole-wrasse, bar jack and the occasional southern-sennet' plus 'moray eels, reef crabs, lobsters') matches this site's location and species list almost verbatim, strongly suggesting it is the same site under a different name used by that source; moray eels, reef crabs, and lobsters are added on that basis, flagged as a name-matched rather than name-identical source. Seahorses and trumpetfish (carried forward from smmainc.com/padi.com, not re-fetched again this cycle) remain unconfirmed for a second audit cycle - flagged for a future pass.

Deep re-audit 2026-09-25. Depth range (18-34m/60-110ft) and stingrays/eagle rays 'abound' reconfirmed via PADI (not re-fetched live today, carried forward as previously verified; tikaye.com returned 503 today so also carried forward). NEW: stolentime.com names 'Anse La Raye' directly and adds jacks, Bermuda chub, spotted drums, and a hedged claim that it is 'probably the best place for spotting turtles' in the area - these were removed in the 2026-07-03 pass as unconfirmed but a genuine (if single) fresh source now supports them, so they are restored with attribution and the source's own hedge preserved. NAMING AMBIGUITY FLAGGED: scubastlucia.com's live page today separately lists a 'Piton Wall' site at the base of Petit Piton whose marine life ('sea whips, gorgonia, delicate soft corals, feather duster worms') closely resembles wording previously attributed here to 'Anse La Raye Wall' - stolentime.com repeats this exact feather-duster-worm phrasing under its own separate 'Piton Wall' entry, not under Anse La Raye. This suggests some cross-listing confusion between two adjacent wall dives (Piton Wall vs. Anse La Raye Wall) across sources; the feather-duster-worm detail has been removed from this site's markdown and the ambiguity is noted explicitly rather than guessed at.

Deep wreck-history re-audit 2026-09-25. Re-fetched divefairhelen.com and scubaweather.com live today (both reconfirm Japanese dredger, purchased early 1990s to dredge Vieux Fort's banana port, scuttled September 1996 by the Department of Fisheries). LENGTH CONFLICT FLAGGED: divefairhelen.com/scubaweather.com give 244 feet (~74-75m); a fresh direct fetch of divingaway.com today instead gives 350+ feet - a real, unresolved conflict between independent sources, written into the markdown rather than picking one figure (244ft treated as the better-corroborated figure since it recurs across more sources). DEPTH CONFLICT FLAGGED: 108ft/33m (divefairhelen.com, scubaweather.com) versus 100ft (divingaway.com) - both noted. ORIENTATION CONFLICT UPDATED: divefairhelen.com again states the vessel 'landed on its side'; divingaway.com's fresh fetch today instead describes a 'trapped air pocket' causing the wreck to flip/turn upside down during the 1996 sinking - this replaces the previously-cited, now-unconfirmable 'Hurricane Lenny' account (still not found by any source today) with a better-documented conflict between 'on its side' and 'upside down,' presented as competing accounts rather than fact. TONNAGE remains omitted - only divefairhelen.com states a figure (16,000 tons), no second source found today. Marine life: eels and barracuda reconfirmed (divefairhelen.com); turtles and large jack schools added as a new, single-source claim from divingaway.com's fresh fetch today, explicitly flagged as not independently corroborated.

Deep re-audit 2026-09-25. scubastlucia.com live fetch today reconfirms sargassum triggerfish in deeper areas and dense sea plume forests as juvenile-fish habitat in the shallows - unchanged from the prior pass. NEW: stolentime.com (fresh domain) independently confirms sargassum triggerfish and adds 'large schools of barracuda,' a more specific detail than the previously-listed 'occasional barracuda'; the markdown has been updated to reflect this more specific, source-backed description.

Deep re-audit 2026-09-25. CORRECTION TO PRIOR CLAIM: the 2026-07-03 pass stated 'no operator website lists a distinctly named site... separate from Superman's Flight or Anse La Raye Wall.' That claim is now known to be inaccurate - both scubastlucia.com's live page and stolentime.com today independently list a distinctly named 'Piton Wall' site at the base of Petit Piton (wall dive, feather duster worms/sea whips/gorgonia), separate from both Superman's Flight and Anse La Raye Wall. However, 'Piton Wall' is described as a WALL dive, not a drift dive, so it does not clearly match this entry's 'drift' site_type or resolve its identity - no coordinates are published by either source to confirm or rule out a match. This entry's site_type is therefore NOT changed (no confirming source for a drift-type identity match), but the description has been rewritten to drop the now-incorrect 'no such site exists' claim and instead accurately describe the open identity question. The underlying drift-diving character of the Piton wall zone remains corroborated via Superman's Flight (a confirmed drift dive at the same headland). Marine life (turtles, stingrays, eagle rays) retained as consistent with the broader Piton wall zone; seahorses/frogfish remain excluded as pinnacle-associated species not confirmed here.

Deep re-audit 2026-09-25. scubastlucia.com live fetch today reconfirms 'a very dramatic dive site with deep water gorgonians and sea whips' and 'huge brain corals and barrel sponges in pristine conditions' - unchanged. divein.com returned no content on a direct re-fetch today (prior 'Great House' Patois translation and big-fish/overfishing note carried forward, not re-verified this cycle). NEW: stolentime.com (fresh domain) independently corroborates the wall structure ('large boulders in the shallows, and a sheer wall below') and, importantly, supplies this site's first genuine site-specific marine-life detail: 'occasionally a large barracuda.' This corrects the 2026-07-03 pass, which stated no site-specific marine life could be verified - that statement is now updated with this single, source-backed detail rather than a fabricated species list.

tags.name: El Pirata Shipwreck
tags.qa_notes: Deep re-audit 2026-09-25 - re-searched again specifically for wreck-history facts (vessel identity, build date, length, tonnage, sinking cause). Found only 'Il Pirata Beach' (a beach near Vieux Fort referenced in a 2025 drowning news article, not a dive source) and a passing WebSearch mention that St Lucia's government purchased 'two old 350+ ft Japanese dredgers' for the Vieux Fort dredging project in the early 1990s (one of which is the well-documented Daini Koyomaru) - this does not establish that El Pirata is the second dredger, and no source names it as such, so this is noted only as an unconfirmed lead, not used as fact. Zero of the five required wreck facts could be cross-checked across 2 independent sources today, same as the prior pass. Remains unvalidated; do not mark validated without a genuine dive-specific or maritime-history source naming this wreck.

tags.name: Fairyland
tags.qa_notes: Deep re-audit 2026-09-25. PADI (nutrient-rich currents, vibrant corals/sponges, schools of fish/rays/turtles/parrotfish/moray eels) and scubastlucia.com (lush nutrient-dense 'magical garden,' plateau 12-18m/40-60ft, lobsters, stingrays, flounders, sea turtles, octopus breeding ground) both reconfirmed. NEW/REVERSAL: stolentime.com (fresh domain) independently confirms 'large numbers of schooling fish, particularly chromes [chromis] and creole wrasse. Turtles are occasionally seen' for a site it names 'Fairy Land' - this reverses the 2026-07-03 pass's removal of chromis and creole wrasse, which are now restored with stolentime.com attribution. Note: scubastlucia.com's live page today groups this site under 'Boat Dives' alongside sites it labels 'Drift dive'; however no source directly states Fairyland's site_type in those words, so site_type remains reef pending clearer confirmation.

tags.name: Maria Island Reef
tags.qa_notes: Deep re-audit 2026-09-25. Re-searched again; still found no dive-operator or dive-database source giving depth, marine life, or difficulty for a named scuba site at Maria Island/Islands. New leads found today (not yet confirmable as this site specifically): a WebSearch synthesis mentions 'Maria Islands' as an offshore dive location near Vieux Fort accessible via the Saint Vincent Passage, reachable through the St. Lucia National Trust's Eco-South Tours, and situated near other southern dive sites named Mathurin Point, Caesar Point (a shipwreck), and Savanne's Bay - none of these leads could be traced to a specific page with verifiable site-specific facts, so they are recorded here as follow-up leads only. Remains unvalidated.
